data.narrative:
Lucid Bots, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Andrew Ashur, Adrian Mayans, and David Danielson, has raised $36.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, and Exotec, all operating in the same sector and stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised ($36M) as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implying a $69M valuation. The peer-median method surveys three direct comparables at Series B stage (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B), yielding a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B–$2.0B.

The triangulation across both methods produces a valuation range of $59M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $910M. The wide spread reflects material tension between capital-deployment-based valuation and market-comparable benchmarking. Key uncertainties include the maturity and revenue profile of peer companies relative to Lucid Bots, the relevance of the single public comparable, and whether the peer set accurately represents achievable market positioning. Additional clarity on product-market fit, revenue traction, and technical differentiation would narrow this range materially.
